mx-1Otq.title: Plants: blue myrtle cactus, short upturned arms
mx-1Otq.summary: Short arms that curve uniformly upward. Abundant in San Luis Potosí and also common in Querétaro and Hidalgo.

mx-2quT.title: Lamp: zig-zag bent arm
mx-2quT.summary: A lamp with a zig-zag bent arm, found in Hermosillo.

mx-2urx.title: Plate: short, many designs
mx-2urx.summary: Short plates in a great variety of designs, and front plates are required. Each state has its own designs (see the plate infographic).

mx-3nP6.title: Plants: saguaro, short curving arms
mx-3nP6.summary: Saguaro cacti grow in the western half of Sonora, with short curving arms from a main trunk.

mx-3pdP.title: Farmland: extremely dark fields
mx-3pdP.summary: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

mx-5mCi.title: Pole: octagonal concrete with engravings
mx-5mCi.summary: Most poles are concrete and eight-sided, often with engravings on the side. Colombia has octagonal poles too.

mx-7E67.title: Plants: huge palm with upright umbrella-like
mx-7E67.summary: Attalea rostrata has upright leaves resembling an umbrella. Mostly in Veracruz and Tabasco, rarely in Chiapas.

mx-7cgL.title: Lamp: black front and back edges, white middle
mx-7cgL.summary: A lamp with black front and back edges and a white middle, found in Santiago de Querétaro.

mx-83dD.title: Bollard: crown and name written on it
mx-83dD.summary: Jalisco bollards sometimes have a crown and the state name on them. Hard to read unless close, but no other bollard here has writing.

mx-8Ipc.title: Crops: sugar cane, most in the east
mx-8Ipc.summary: Sugar cane grows nationwide but by far the most in Veracruz.

mx-8VA3.title: Google car: white truck with visible mirrors
mx-8VA3.summary: A white truck with visible rearview mirrors in the Cofre de Perote national park.

mx-8Vzg.title: Soil: blindingly white
mx-8Vzg.summary: Almost blindingly white soil on the Yucatán peninsula, most common in Quintana Roo. Only consistent in Gen 3.

mx-8Yrh.title: Roofs: thatched
mx-8Yrh.summary: Thatched roofs are most common on the Yucatán peninsula and in eastern San Luis Potosí, and found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

mx-9nVQ.title: Plants: small bright silver-grey shrubs
mx-9nVQ.summary: Brittlebush is a small shrub with bright silver-grey leaves, most common in Sonora especially around Hermosillo.

mx-AkFp.title: Crops: oil palm plantations
mx-AkFp.summary: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the edges in Veracruz, Tabasco and Campeche.

mx-CdsA.title: Landscape: rocky pine mountains
mx-CdsA.summary: West Chihuahua and Durango can be rocky and mountainous with pine forests. The pines are shorter and more stunted than in the centre or south.

mx-Cits.title: Plants: boojum tree, alien tentacle look
mx-Cits.summary: Boojum trees look alien and tentacle-like. Almost only in the southern half of Baja California.

mx-EuEs.title: Plants: citrus plantations on hilltops
mx-EuEs.summary: Around Poza Rica in Veracruz many citrus plantations, often grown right on top of hills.

mx-FGDc.title: Walls: light-coloured rock
mx-FGDc.summary: Walls of light-coloured rock on the Yucatán peninsula, most common in Yucatán state. They look darker out of the sun.

mx-GyUQ.title: Houses: mud brick, whole houses
mx-GyUQ.summary: Mud brick buildings are most common in Durango, especially entire houses, and appear in almost all the dry desert states.

mx-Hv5a.title: Houses: white concrete blocks around the
mx-Hv5a.summary: White concrete block buildings are concentrated in the states around Mexico City, more to the east, but found everywhere.

mx-I66z.title: Google car: yellow hood
mx-I66z.summary: A Street View car with a yellow hood near La Malinche volcano in Tlaxcala.

mx-IdEs.title: Pole: lowered crossbar with a single brace
mx-IdEs.summary: Poles with a lowered crossbar and one support beam running from one end of the crossbar to the pole, found in Durango.

mx-K8qz.title: Landscape: extremely long flat ridge
mx-K8qz.summary: An extremely long, flat ridge in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosí.

mx-KwCu.title: Road: divided highway, yucca on both sides
mx-KwCu.summary: The 54 is a divided highway through northeastern Zacatecas with yucca trees on both sides. The Street View car is often exposed and looks almost white in the sun.

mx-LMob.title: Shops: OXXO and Pemex
mx-LMob.summary: OXXO and Pemex are two of the most popular fuel and convenience brands. OXXO can still be found, less often, in other countries.

mx-LWLO.title: Sign: very thick arrows
mx-LWLO.summary: Arrows on signs are noticeably thick, compared with other countries in the Americas.

mx-Lc0Z.title: Road: lush cliffs, tunnels
mx-Lc0Z.summary: The 40D across the Sinaloa-Durango line has lush cliffs and mountains, frequent tunnels and double yellow centre lines.

mx-M4Ya.title: Ground: hexagonal tile paving
mx-M4Ya.summary: Pavement of hexagonal tiles is in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

mx-MIDc.title: Lamp: rectangular head with ring bulb
mx-MIDc.summary: A lamp with a rectangular head and ring-shaped bulb, found in Matamoros.

mx-MIKv.title: Taxi: white lower half, pink upper half
mx-MIKv.summary: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half and a pink upper half.

mx-MkKr.title: Houses: round electricity meters
mx-MkKr.summary: Round electricity meters are used. The US, Guatemala, Dominican Republic and the Philippines have them too.

mx-MwVY.title: Pole: white paint strip with street name
mx-MwVY.summary: Poles in Chihuahua city sometimes have a white paint strip with the street name in black or blue.

mx-Mziq.title: Ground: messy irregular cobblestone
mx-Mziq.summary: Unorganised cobblestone with irregular tiles is in most central states, but most common in Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Querétaro.

mx-N0AG.title: Houses: red brick, mostly west of the capital
mx-N0AG.summary: Red brick buildings are concentrated in the states west of Mexico City: Jalisco, Michoacán, Guanajuato and Aguascalientes.

mx-O9Bd.title: Landscape: orange-soil dirt roads, low shrubs
mx-O9Bd.summary: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez have lots of dirt roads with a distinct orange soil and low shrubs.

mx-ORWw.title: Crops: vast fields of blue agave
mx-ORWw.summary: Vast fields of blue agave (for tequila), mostly in Jalisco and Nayarit.

mx-Ok3w.title: Plants: sabal palm, lollipop sun-shaped crown
mx-Ok3w.summary: Sabal palms are mostly on the east coast, the Yucatán peninsula and Nayarit, with a spiky, sun-shaped crown like a lollipop.

mx-PNuD.title: Bollard: red band near the top
mx-PNuD.summary: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, with one exception: Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

mx-QJWC.title: Plants: prickly pear with flat oval pads
mx-QJWC.summary: Prickly pear cacti have flat, oval pads. They are noticeably more common in the centre and rarely seen in the south and coastal states.

mx-RbcF.title: Ground: three lines of cobblestone pattern
mx-RbcF.summary: This exact paving with three lines of cobblestone patterning is mainly in Oaxaca.

mx-RddA.title: Road: grainy blue-grey pavement
mx-RddA.summary: Grainy pavement with a bluish-grey tinge is common in Tamaulipas and Nuevo León. In Tamaulipas larger roads often have dashed outer lines.

mx-Rr0V.title: Plants: tree yucca, oblong rosettes on a trunk
mx-Rr0V.summary: Yucca filifera (tree yucca) and Y. decipiens, mostly in San Luis Potosí and Zacatecas and some bordering northern states. Oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves on a single tree-like trunk.

mx-RrIm.title: Pole: wooden with a lowered crossbar
mx-RrIm.summary: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly in Sinaloa and Sonora.

mx-Rttz.title: Pole: bottom half painted green
mx-Rttz.summary: The lower half of poles in Cuernavaca is often painted green. In Gen 4 the paint looks faded, sometimes barely visible.

mx-Ryu4.title: Pole: wooden version with hanging insulators
mx-Ryu4.summary: The wooden version of the hanging pole is on the Baja California peninsula.

mx-SUto.title: Google car: white Gen 3
mx-SUto.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage mainly shows two cars: a white car with a stubby antenna wrapped in a diagonal coil, and a white car with a more visible back and a long red brake light instead of an antenna. You may also see a white car with only a tiny sliver where the antenna should be.

mx-UPKI.title: Rooftops: wide cylindrical black or white
mx-UPKI.summary: Wide cylindrical black or white water tanks are often on rooftops.

mx-VvCA.title: Place names: lots of x, tl, -ec, -tlan
mx-VvCA.summary: Many place names come from Nahuatl, with plenty of x and tl and endings like -ec and -tlan.

mx-WhQo.title: Road: yellow accents on kerbs and bridge
mx-WhQo.summary: Yellow marking on kerbs and bridge barriers is quite common.

mx-X6cJ.title: Plants: pulque agave
mx-X6cJ.summary: Agave salmiana has wide, smooth, curling leaves in a crown shape. Common in the central valley and further north around San Luis Potosí.

mx-XsTl.title: Landscape: tall flat ridge with prominent
mx-XsTl.summary: A tall flat ridge in the Maderas del Carmen reserve in northern Coahuila near the US border, seen only from Federal Highway 53.

differs.how: Near the US border but only seen from one highway

mx-YJOx.title: Road lines: white centre line
mx-YJOx.summary: White centre lines are most common in Tabasco.

mx-Yn3G.title: Landscape: reddish-brown hills with big
mx-Yn3G.summary: Reddish-brown hills often with large boulders are common in the northern half of Baja California.

mx-Z8y6.title: Road divider: yellow top and bottom edge
mx-Z8y6.summary: A road divider with yellow top and bottom edges runs along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.

mx-aRyM.title: Landmark: rows of wind turbines
mx-aRyM.summary: The Eurus Wind Farm in southeast Oaxaca is the largest in the country. Rows of turbines line the 190 around Juchitán de Zaragoza.

mx-ah2z.title: Plate: every state has its own design
mx-ah2z.summary: Each state has one or more unique plate designs. The infographic shows the most common and helpful ones.

mx-baRr.title: Sign back: thick cross
mx-baRr.summary: A thick cross on the back of road signs in Chihuahua.

mx-cAuJ.title: Plants: thin white-barked trees
mx-cAuJ.summary: Thin trees with white bark on the Yucatán peninsula, most common in Quintana Roo.

mx-caRa.title: Fences: living trees with red bark
mx-caRa.summary: Fences made of trees with red-coloured bark are common in Veracruz. They also occur in other coastal states, so combine with other clues.

mx-ctfG.title: Sign: stop sign reading ALTO
mx-ctfG.summary: Stop signs say "ALTO". Panama, Costa Rica and Guatemala use it too. All of South America and Puerto Rico say "PARE".

mx-cx4K.title: Plants: many kinds of cacti everywhere
mx-cx4K.summary: Cacti of many species are extremely common.

mx-cxcn.title: Farmland: red agricultural fields
mx-cxcn.summary: Red farm fields are common in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

mx-duJ1.title: Landscape: jagged cliffs, pinkish soil
mx-duJ1.summary: Around Guaymas: jagged cliffs and mountains, distinctly pinkish soil, and organ pipe cacti on the hills and beside the road.

mx-eOQI.title: Farmland: red fields among dense tropical
mx-eOQI.summary: Red farm fields surrounded by dense tropical forest, most common in northern Campeche.

mx-fEc6.title: Bollard: small white cylinder, black base
mx-fEc6.summary: A small, cylindrical white bollard with a black base, unique here. A yellow reflector is sometimes seen, and there is also a flat version.

mx-gENZ.title: Road lines: black tar on both sides of yellow
mx-gENZ.summary: Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line appears in Sinaloa, Durango and Guerrero. Most reliable when the tar is not faded.

mx-gFf9.title: Google car: red with black roof
mx-gFf9.summary: A red Street View car with a black roof in the town of La Seca in Sinaloa.

mx-gmje.title: Road lines: white edges
mx-gmje.summary: The typical lines are solid white edges with a single unbroken yellow centre line. A single broken yellow centre or double yellow centre are also common.

mx-gtmC.title: Phone numbers: first digit shows the region
mx-gtmC.summary: The first digit of area codes is regional. See the map.

mx-gyjK.title: Plants: organ pipe
mx-gyjK.summary: Organ pipe cacti have long thin stems sprouting near ground level. Most common in Sonora and occasionally Baja California Sur.

mx-hFJl.title: Pole: concrete
mx-hFJl.summary: Concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatán peninsula.

mx-hWCI.title: Sign: large all-caps white direction font
mx-hWCI.summary: Direction signs use a distinctly large, all-caps white font.

mx-hlxm.title: Plants: gold grass tufts in a line by the road
mx-hlxm.summary: Gold tufts of grass in a line right by the road are most common in Coahuila.

mx-htqU.title: Cars: lots of US brands and pickups
mx-htqU.summary: US car brands are popular, with a lot of pickup trucks.

mx-iMLc.title: Pole: asymmetric crossbar
mx-iMLc.summary: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are only in Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo and Morelos.

mx-jCer.title: Plants: coconut palms in coastal groups
mx-jCer.summary: Coconut palms grow all along the coast, often in big groups in Guerrero and Colima.

mx-jhvW.title: Pole: white acorn-shaped insulators
mx-jhvW.summary: White acorn-shaped insulators appear in coastal states, most of all in Michoacán, Colima and Veracruz.

mx-l5bZ.title: Landscape: tall mountain ranges surrounding a
mx-l5bZ.summary: The Monterrey area is ringed by tall, striking mountain ranges.

mx-l7RV.title: Google car: Gen 4, visible front, blue
mx-l7RV.summary: Newer Gen 4 cars often show the front and come in several colour schemes. The three most common are blue, white with a blue stripe, and black.

mx-lXCZ.title: Google car: Gen 2 coverage exists
mx-lXCZ.summary: One of very few Latin American countries with the older Gen 2 camera (lower quality). Brazil has some but much rarer, since most was overwritten.

mx-lm-2589.title: Pole: black-yellow barberpole or tall
mx-lm-2589.summary: In Jalisco, poles are often painted in a Taiwan-style black and yellow barberpole or in a Kansai-style with long vertical black and yellow stripes. They can very rarely appear in other states.

differs.how: Taiwan has similar poles, but this is a different region

mx-lm-483069.title: Farmland: neat rows of pulque agave
mx-lm-483069.summary: Scattered farms of pulque agave, in neat rows stretching endlessly, almost always around Pachuca in Hidalgo and rarely further southeast.

mx-lm-483070.title: Plants: slightly less blue agave, small groups
mx-lm-483070.summary: A blue agave, but less blue than the tequila one, in smaller groups. Found in central Oaxaca.

mx-lm-483071.title: Plants: slick lime-green agave
mx-lm-483071.summary: Agave lechuguilla is common in the hills of Durango and Coahuila, especially around Saltillo and west of Torreón, more rarely San Luis Potosí and Hidalgo. Slick lime-green leaves that look combed to one side.

mx-lm-483072.title: Plants: small bluish agave, hard to spot
mx-lm-483072.summary: The rough century plant looks like the pulque agave but is bluish and much smaller. It has nearly the same range as lechuguilla (Durango, Coahuila around Saltillo and west of Torreón), and is often only barely visible in batches in the distance.

mx-lm-483073.title: Plants: agave with thin spiky cylindrical leaf
mx-lm-483073.summary: A. karwinskii is only in the central desert of Oaxaca, mostly near Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz. Spiky thin leaves in a cylindrical shape set it apart from other agaves.

mx-lm-483074.title: Plants: cup-shaped agave on walls
mx-lm-483074.summary: Agave cupreata is very rare and found in central Guerrero. It has a pronounced cup shape with leaves curving inwards, often growing in groups on walls.

mx-lm-587153.title: Farmland: prickly pear plantations on plains
mx-lm-587153.summary: In the far northeast of the State of Mexico around Nopaltepec, prickly pear is farmed in vast plains. Otherwise most common in northeast Morelos in front of eroded dry hills, and possibly Guanajuato third.

mx-lm-587202.title: Plants: only prickly pear, no other succulents
mx-lm-587202.summary: Prickly pear with no other cacti, yucca, agaves or succulents is generally a good sign of the centre-west: Jalisco, Guanajuato or Michoacán.

mx-lm-587204.title: Plants: huge numbers of organ pipe cacti
mx-lm-587204.summary: An abundance of organ pipe cacti usually means the El Cajón del Diablo reserve, south of Hermosillo.

mx-lm-587205.title: Plants: tree cholla in groups
mx-lm-587205.summary: Tree cholla in groups is usually a good sign of San Luis Potosí.

mx-lm-587206.title: Plants: odd cactus you can't identify
mx-lm-587206.summary: Oaxaca is very diverse in cacti, so a strange cactus not covered elsewhere suggests Oaxaca.

mx-lm-587207.title: Plants: cactus right by the coast
mx-lm-587207.summary: A cactus in a coastal area probably means Oaxaca.

mx-lm-587208.title: Plants: tall unbranched columnar cactus
mx-lm-587208.summary: A tall columnar cactus with no branches, native to northern Oaxaca and southern Puebla, less commonly central Guerrero.

mx-lm-587209.title: Plants: dense branches
mx-lm-587209.summary: The Indian comb (Pachycereus pecten-aboriginum) always suggests Sinaloa or south Sonora near Sinaloa. Dense branches from one stem and bright flowers at the tips of the arms.

mx-lm-587210.title: Plants: palm with round fan leaves
mx-lm-587210.summary: Florida thatch palm has round fan leaves and is usually found in Yucatán within Mexico.

mx-lm-97305.title: Plants: palm with large stiff pointy leaves
mx-lm-97305.summary: Sabal mexicana has large, stiff, pointy, densely packed leaves. Found in the east and south coast, the Yucatán and Guatemala. Sabal yapa droops and looks shredded; sabal rosei has visible gaps and brighter green leaves.

mx-lm-97306.title: Plants: palm with visible leaf gaps
mx-lm-97306.summary: Sabal rosei grows on the Pacific coast, from Sinaloa to Jalisco, mostly in Nayarit. Its leaves have visible gaps and a brighter green than the other sabal palms.

mx-lm-97333.title: Plants: palm with drooping, shredded-tip leaves
mx-lm-97333.summary: Sabal yapa grows almost only on the Yucatán peninsula. Its leaves droop and look shredded at the tips.

mx-lm-97372.title: Plants: candelabra cactus
mx-lm-97372.summary: Pachycereus weberi is widespread in Puebla, Guerrero, Morelos, Hidalgo and Oaxaca at 600 to 1,500 m.

mx-lm-97373.title: Plants: chiotilla cactus
mx-lm-97373.summary: Native to Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca and southern Puebla. Seeing it almost always means Oaxaca, usually central.

mx-lm-97374.title: Plants: golden glowing fruit cholla
mx-lm-97374.summary: The fruit cholla has an unmistakable golden glow and is mostly in the western half of Sonora.

mx-lm-97375.title: Plants: pitaya with branches curling from a
mx-lm-97375.summary: Branches curl smoothly outwards from a central stem, unlike the weed-like organ pipe. Mostly south of Guadalajara in Jalisco, less often Guanajuato, and surprisingly rarely Querétaro.

mx-lm-97376.title: Plants: tall cactus with thin twirling branches
mx-lm-97376.summary: A rare tall cactus (Stenocereus fricii) with thin, twirling branches, unique to Michoacán and very abundant on the 37D.

mx-lm-97377.title: Plants: tree cholla, skeletal discoloured arms
mx-lm-97377.summary: Tree cholla has skeletal, discoloured arms sprouting in every direction. Mostly in San Luis Potosí, Querétaro and Hidalgo, often in Coahuila and Durango, rarely in Zacatecas.

mx-loiN.title: Road: white km markers, black text and outline
mx-loiN.summary: Kilometre markers are white with black lettering and outline, set at hip height with "km" and the number stacked vertically.

mx-lwNA.title: Pole: mesh body
mx-lwNA.summary: Poles with a mesh body are most common in San Luis Potosí, Guanajuato and Querétaro.

mx-md8U.title: Landmark: pink lakes
mx-md8U.summary: Las Coloradas is famous for the pink lakes around the area.

mx-or0C.title: Landscape: flat farmland, ridge west
mx-or0C.summary: Around Mexicali: flat farmland with a ridge to the west, very common Washingtonia palms and brown wooden poles.

mx-p6Xz.title: Landscape: rolling hills alternating orange
mx-p6Xz.summary: Around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south in Oaxaca, rolling hills with distinct orange and beige soil that changes with each hill.

mx-pAC6.title: Lamp: five round bulbs like a dice
mx-pAC6.summary: A lamp with five round bulbs that looks like a dice face, found in Cancún.

mx-q149.title: Landscape: twin volcanoes
mx-q149.summary: The twin volcanoes Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl sit on the border of the State of Mexico and Puebla. They are usually much less visible than in the reference photo.

mx-qDSL.title: Road shields: curvy national
mx-qDSL.summary: Two shields: national highways have a slightly curvy shape with the country name on top, and state roads have straight borders, usually with state initials on top.

mx-sf65.title: Postal codes: on street signs
mx-sf65.summary: Postal codes usually appear at the bottom of street signs and are ordered alphabetically by state name. See the map.

mx-u1UV.title: Plants: giant cardon, sprawling arms, ribbed
mx-u1UV.summary: The giant cardon is extremely common in Baja California: large sprawling arms from one ribbed trunk.

mx-vK3L.title: Lamp: black rectangular head
mx-vK3L.summary: A lamp with a black rectangular head, found in Cuernavaca.

mx-vOyN.title: Landscape: distinct extinct volcano
mx-vOyN.summary: Cerro del Bernal, a distinct extinct volcano in southern Tamaulipas, northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.

mx-vZJe.title: Plants: teardrop-shaped grass clumps
mx-vZJe.summary: Clumps of grass shaped almost like teardrops, common around Tlaxcala.

mx-xzN2.title: Lamp posts: mostly yellow
mx-xzN2.summary: Most lamp posts and arms in Aguascalientes city are yellow. Not exclusive, just very common.

mx-yUfA.title: Houses: US bungalow style, pastel, gated
mx-yUfA.summary: In the north, houses borrow from American bungalows: light or pastel colours, gates and front yards, plus orange Spanish-colonial style tiles.

mx-zF4Y.title: Landscape: pinkish-tan soil and canals around
mx-zF4Y.summary: Around Ciudad Obregón: pinkish-tan soil and canals around the farmland.
